functionalReqs: Run jobs on a pool of workers
hints: If one scheduler process scans for due jobs, what happens when it dies? And if two run?
Partition jobs across scheduler nodes, and give workers leases (visibility timeouts) on claimed runs.

Jobs table indexed by next_run_time and partitioned; scheduler nodes own partitions (via leader election or consistent hashing), push due runs to a queue; workers claim with a lease and heartbeat; expired leases are retried; idempotency guidance for job authors; top-of-hour spikes smoothed with jitter.
nonFunctionalReqs: Jobs start within seconds of their scheduled time
No job silently skipped; duplicates minimised
Scales to millions of jobs per day
problemStatement:
Design a **distributed job scheduler** (like a hosted cron or Airflow's scheduler): users register jobs that run once at a time or on a schedule, and the system runs them on a worker fleet.

Every job must run on time and exactly once from the user's point of view, even when machines die.

scaleHints.qps: ~10M job runs per day, bursts at the top of each minute/hour

title: Design a Distributed Job Scheduler
